label: nyiso 238 hydro budget
definition: KEEPER. The superseded keeper's frozen recipe with EXACTLY ONE ScenarioConfig field changed: hydro_budget_period_by_instrument False -> True. The LP's hydro row conserves energy over a period that defaults to the calendar month, letting a plant bank water across ~730 hours at zero cost; this arm shortens that period to the one each project's OWN GOVERNING INSTRUMENT permits - Niagara (EIA 2693) to 24 h (1950 Niagara Diversion Treaty + INBC 1993 Directive state no conservation period, and the plant has 0.244 h of measured NID forebay pondage, so undiverted water goes over the Falls) and St Lawrence (EIA 2694) to 168 h (IJC 2016-12-08 Supplementary Order's WEEKLY regulation plan plus the peaking-and-ponding directive, stated in words). ZERO free parameters, neither duration swept. The 161 remaining NYISO hydro plants keep the monthly period - their FERC licence articles have not been read, and rule 14 forbids inventing an instrument. AGAINST THE SUPERSEDED KEEPER, EXACTLY ONE SCORED CRITERION MOVES AND IT MOVES THE RIGHT WAY: C3a mean LMP 2022 FAIL -> PASS. Nothing flips PASS -> FAIL. SHAPE, against the EIA-930 meter: hydro hourly r 0.6851->0.7738, 0.6682->0.7235, 0.7313->0.7782, 0.7127->0.7906 for 2022/23/24/25, and the GAS fleet's own hourly fit improves in every year on both metrics (r +0.0017/+0.0020/+0.0010/+0.0071, NRMSE -0.0013/-0.0020/-0.0005/-0.0040) - 16 of 16 directional wins, small in magnitude but uniform in sign and the sign the mechanism predicts. COST, STATED NOT HIDDEN: the mechanism's own pre-registered G2 identity gate (annual hydro within 0.1 %) FAILS in 2022 (-0.2155 %, -55.2 GWh) and 2023 (-0.0957 %, -25.5 GWh) and passes in 2024/2025 (0.0000 %). Promoted on the OWNER'S RULING that structural integrity may outweigh a gate regression. The G2 loss is an OPEN ROOT-CAUSE ISSUE, not an accepted limitation: the LP declines to run Niagara when Upstate_West is priced <= $0 (498 h in 2022 against a measured 21-127) and a 24 h use-it-or-lose-it budget cannot move that water. nyiso-238's phase 0 killed ALL FOUR candidates for that price fabrication at zero LP, so it has no identifiable repair in the five-zone representation. Run-level NOT-YET is 2022-driven (fuelmix CC_REGULAR +4.81 TWh, and the C3c scarcity tail this model class does not form); the ISO's 2023-2025 tier determination is unchanged. Evidence: docs/RESULT-nyiso238-hydro-budget-span-2026-09-16.md; docs/PRECOMMIT-nyiso238-hydro-budget-span-2026-09-16.md (pushed before the first LP).
market_story: HYDRO: Niagara and St Lawrence are treaty-and-licence water, not fuel. Niagara's diversion is set hour by hour by the 1950 Treaty's scenic-flow schedule and the plant holds only ~15 minutes of forebay, so water it does not run goes over the Falls within the day - it cannot be saved for a better-priced week. St Lawrence is the opposite case by its own instrument: the IJC's weekly regulation plan plus an explicit peaking-and-ponding directive let it shift water within the week but require the weekly total to hold. Giving the LP a calendar-month budget let both plants bank water across ~730 hours at zero cost, which no instrument permits and which shows up in the meter as hydro run in the wrong hours. GAS: that mis-timed hydro was displacing gas. New York's upstate hydro is inframarginal, so an hour where the model runs banked water is an hour it does not run the combined cycle the market actually dispatched. Constraining each project to its own instrument's period puts the water back where the licence puts it, and the gas fleet's hourly fit against EIA-930 improves in all four years as a consequence - not because anything about gas was tuned.
